questions.q: How is a measure's value calculated?
options: Dynamically, based on whatever is filtering it at the moment — nothing is stored
Once, when the formula is entered, and stored for every row
Only when the file is first created
Measures are calculated identically to calculated columns
questions.explain: A measure recalculates fresh every time the filter context changes — slicers, drill-downs, or any other filter — unlike a calculated column's stored, row-by-row values.

questions.q: What icon marks a measure in the Data pane?
options: A calculator icon
A table icon
A funnel icon
A magnifying glass icon
questions.explain: Measures you create appear in the Data pane with a calculator icon, distinguishing them from plain columns and implicit summarizations.

questions.q: In 'Projected Sales = SUM(\'Reseller Sales\'[Last Years Sales])*1.06', what does this measure calculate?
options: Last year's sales total, increased by 6%
The average of last year's sales
A count of sales transactions
The difference between this year and last year's sales
questions.explain: The formula sums Last Years Sales and multiplies the result by 1.06 — a 6% projected increase.

options: The table a measure is filed under in the Data pane, which can be reassigned
The table the measure's data was originally imported from
The first table created in the model
A special hidden table Power BI creates automatically
questions.explain: A measure's home table determines where it's listed in the Data pane — modelers can reassign it wherever makes the most sense for report authors.

questions.q: What's a useful way to learn DAX patterns using quick measures?
options: Create a quick measure through its dialog, then open it afterward to read the DAX formula Power BI generated
Quick measures can't be inspected — they're hidden from the model
Quick measures always use calculated columns, not measures
Quick measures require writing DAX manually first
questions.explain: Quick measures are configured through a dialog with no DAX typing required, but the resulting formula is fully visible and editable afterward — a good way to see working examples of common patterns.
